title: Living in Japan: read six survival signs and places
description: Read essential station signs, medical places, and city hall terms in hiragana for everyday life in Japan.

review.provenance: Independently authored short daily-survival cues and explanations; common Japanese sign and institution spellings and meanings are linguistic facts.
review.rightsBasis: Original agent-written prompts, translations, contexts and explanations; no copied text, audio or third-party assets.

reviewItems.skill: Read 入口 (entrance) on building and station signs
Read 出口 (exit) on transit signs
Read 病院 (hospital/clinic) when seeking medical care
Read 薬局 (pharmacy) when picking up medicine
Read 市役所 (city hall) for resident registration
Read 住所 (address) on resident and housing forms

exercises.prompt: Outside a station or municipal building, read this sign marking where to enter and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Follow the entrance sign into a building or station.

text.context: Follow the entrance sign into a building or station.

exercises.explanation: 入口 is read いりぐち and means entrance; 口 becomes voiced ぐち in this compound.

exercises.prompt: Inside a train station, read this yellow sign pointing the way out and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Check which station exit is closest to your destination.

text.context: Check which station exit is closest to your destination.

exercises.explanation: 出口 is read でぐち and means exit; station signs across Japan pair 出口 with exit numbers or directions.

exercises.prompt: When you feel unwell and need to see a doctor, read this word and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Look for a hospital or medical clinic in your neighborhood.

text.context: Look for a hospital or medical clinic in your neighborhood.

exercises.explanation: 病院 is read びょういん and means hospital or medical clinic; note contracted びょ followed by う.

exercises.prompt: After receiving a prescription or looking for cold medicine, read this storefront sign and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Bring a prescription to the pharmacy.

text.context: Bring a prescription to the pharmacy.

exercises.explanation: 薬局 is read やっきょく and means pharmacy; small っ doubles the k sound before contracted きょ.

exercises.prompt: When registering your address after moving to Japan, read this municipal office name and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Visit city hall to submit a resident registration form.

text.context: Visit city hall to submit a resident registration form.

exercises.explanation: 市役所 is read しやくしょ and means city hall or municipal office; note full-sized や in やく and small ょ in しょ.

exercises.prompt: On a resident registration or apartment application form, read this field label for where you live and type its reading in hiragana.

stimulus.context: Write your current address on a city hall or bank form.

text.context: Write your current address on a city hall or bank form.

exercises.explanation: 住所 is read じゅうしょ and means residential address; じゅ is lengthened by う.
